_fixture_note: Sanitized — resolves the P1 'cancel endpoint behavior' unknown from marianatek.md §1F. Production account, 2026-07-02. Covers both a self-booking cancel and a guest-booking cancel; both zero-penalty, well within the free-cancellation window.

step1_cancel_penalty_check._note: Always call this before cancelling — it's read-only/safe and tells you whether the cancel will incur a penalty. This matches the shape already documented in §1D from the original June 22 test-account research; this round confirms it against a real chargeable membership account.

response_body_key_fields.class_session_available_spot_count: incremented back up by 1 (20 -> 21 in this capture)

step2_cancel_self_booking._note: Cancelling a STANDARD (non-waitlist) booking sets status to "standard cancel" — distinct from the waitlist cancel status below.

step3_cancel_guest_booking.critical_finding: The user's *own* membership.guest_remaining_usage_count went 2 (before booking) -> 1 (after booking the guest) -> 2 (after cancelling the guest booking, zero-penalty). This CONFIRMS membership usage/allowance IS restored on a zero-penalty cancel — it is not just 'no fee charged', the underlying usage count itself reverts. This directly answers the open question the stakeholder asked us to resolve via production-account capture (does cancelling inside the free window give the credit/usage back, or just avoid a fee).
